gen-dafont-visitor-gf-roboto: Roboto keeps its round letters generously open, a clean foil to Visitor, whose strokes look pulled like solder through a nozzle. Let the sans body run a touch larger than feels natural.
gen-dafont-visitor-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its mean line high, a modern counterpart to Visitor's nostalgic digital look. Down a full page of text, the sans-serif moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-vogue-fs-epilogue: Wiry, curvy and unclamped, Epilogue reads approachable while Vogue swings between stout beams and fine threads. Line after line, that single wire-like stroke keeps the reading light and unhurried.
gen-dafont-vogue-fs-fira-sans: Clean to its core, Fira Sans opens its s curves wide at both ends, while Vogue carries hairline serifs on heavy stems. Its large x-height makes whole paragraphs feel open and unhurried.
gen-dafont-wanted-m54-fs-bespoke-sans: Curves pinched shut like squeezed wire define Wanted M54. That look carries frontier swagger best, while Bespoke Sans keeps curve ends wide of the stem for a sharp, refined finish.
gen-dafont-wanted-m54-fs-rowan: Pinched loops on one side, open curves on the other. Wanted M54 is best at vintage frontier punch, while Rowan, a literary and friendly serif, suits brief bursts of text.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-hoover: Wide channels, towering lowercase, and nothing timid about it. Woodgod commands attention with vintage swagger, while Hoover, a refined, robust serif with compressed ascenders, handles the quieter supporting work.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Heavy vintage swagger, then a soft landing below. Woodgod brings vintage force up top, while Pilcrow Rounded packs big counters and open, unclosed curves into a warm, tidy sans.
gen-dafont-woodgod-sora: Sora keeps its c and s widely parted and its curves free of pressure swell, a precise counterpoint to Woodgod's wide channels. The geometric sans-serif stays quiet and lets the vintage heading take the lead.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-public-sans: Heavy stems joined by thread-thin arms give DM Serif Text a bookish, editorial bite right away. And Public Sans, a hefty sans-serif with broad open counters, settles in underneath with trustworthy, low-key weight.
